complex-variable-and-transform-technique.title: Cauchy-Riemann from two approach paths
steps: \Delta z=i\Delta y:\quad f'=\frac{u_{y}\Delta y+iv_{y}\Delta y}{i\Delta y}=v_{y}-iu_{y}
complex-variable-and-transform-technique.note: The derivative must be path independent, so the real-axis and imaginary-axis limits have to agree term by term.

complex-variable-and-transform-technique.title: Analytic functions satisfy Laplace's equation
symbols: real and imaginary parts of f
complex-variable-and-transform-technique.note: Equality of the mixed partials is the only extra fact needed, and it holds because v is itself smooth.

complex-variable-and-transform-technique.title: Residue at a pole of order n
complex-variable-and-transform-technique.note: Multiplying by (z - z0)^n makes the series regular, and n-1 derivatives kill every term except the residue one.

complex-variable-and-transform-technique.title: Types of isolated singularity
rows: f tends to the finite value a0
complex-variable-and-transform-technique.note: Only the principal part decides the type: removable can be patched, a pole blows up like a power, an essential one does neither.

complex-variable-and-transform-technique.title: Standard Laplace pairs
complex-variable-and-transform-technique.note: Every entry is the same integral evaluated on one prototype; the ROC column is what makes the inverse unique.

complex-variable-and-transform-technique.title: Coefficients from orthogonality
steps: \text{multiply }f\text{ by }\cos m\omega_{0}t\text{ and integrate over one period}
symbols: fundamental period, with omega0 = 2 pi / T
complex-variable-and-transform-technique.note: Orthogonality makes every other harmonic integrate to zero, so each coefficient can be extracted independently of the rest.

complex-variable-and-transform-technique.title: Delay becomes an exponential factor
symbols: step that switches the function on at t = a
complex-variable-and-transform-technique.note: The step is what makes the lower limit a instead of 0, and the substitution then pulls the exponential out as a pure factor.
